visual_action: A montage-style political ad for Kamala Harris. It begins with B-roll of nature, a train crossing a bridge, and diverse Americans at work (mechanic, farm workers). It then cuts to clips of Kamala Harris campaigning, getting off a plane with Tim Walz, exiting a campaign bus, and meeting with supporters in various settings like a shop and with a football team. There are numerous shots of large, diverse crowds at rallies holding signs for "HARRIS WALZ" and with slogans like "FREEDOM" and "A NEW WAY FORWARD". The montage continues with shots of working-class Americans, an officer's hat, and more rally footage, including men wearing "OLD WHITE MEN FOR HARRIS" t-shirts. Harris is shown speaking at a podium and waving to crowds. The ad uses editing effects like a film reel border and a torn-paper split-screen to show different people side-by-side. The ad concludes with Harris at a podium with text reading "A NEW WAY FORWARD VOTE BY NOVEMBER 5" and a final shot of her and Tim Walz waving on stage.

cast.name: Kamala Harris
cast.evidence: Kamala Harris is the central figure of the ad, shown speaking, campaigning, and featured in on-screen text that identifies it as her ad.

cast.name: Tim Walz
cast.evidence: He is shown alongside Kamala Harris on stage and on the campaign bus, and his name appears on campaign materials like the bus and signs ("HARRIS WALZ").

A NEW WAY FORWARD
VOTE BY NOVEMBER 5
HARRIS WALZ
PAID FOR BY HARRIS FOR PRESIDENT

spoken_summary: The ad intersperses clips of Kamala Harris speaking with the lyrics of the song "Wake Up Everybody." Harris says, "This is going to be a tight race until the very end. We have some hard work ahead of us... Things are different... With your help, we are going to win this November... Liberty for each of us depends on liberty for all of us." The song lyrics include lines like "Wake up everybody, no more sleepin' in bed," "No more backward thinkin', time for thinkin' ahead," "The world has changed so very much," and "The world won't get no better if we just let it be... we got to change it, yeah, just you and me."
audio_music: The entire ad is set to the upbeat, soulful 1975 song "Wake Up Everybody" by Harold Melvin & The Blue Notes. The song's hopeful and socially conscious lyrics drive the ad's inspirational and urgent tone.
editing_pacing: The ad is a fast-paced montage with quick cuts between campaign footage, B-roll of diverse Americans, and large rally crowds. It employs stylized visual effects like a film-strip border on some clips and a torn-paper split-screen effect.
cultural_references: The song "Wake Up Everybody" by Harold Melvin & The Blue Notes (featuring Teddy Pendergrass).
central_claim: The Harris-Walz campaign represents a hopeful, inclusive path forward for America, but winning a tight election against backward-looking forces will require everyone to get involved and vote.
intended_effect: To inspire and mobilize voters for the Harris-Walz ticket by presenting their campaign as an energetic, positive, and necessary movement for the country's future.
